sections.what: Maps risk levels to badge colours, then for each project shows its name, a risk badge, its description, its velocity, and a completion bar.

sections.name: ProjectHealthView (part 2)
sections.title: Sprint burndown chart and empty state
sections.what: Draws a line chart for each project with two lines: a dashed grey ideal line and a solid indigo actual line with dots. Shows a message card when there are no projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: the dashed line is the target and the solid line is real progress, so the gap between them is visible.
sections.watch_out: The chart reads fields named day, ideal and actual. Data with other names shows an empty chart.

summary: Shows each project's health: risk level, velocity, a completion bar, and a sprint burndown line chart.
purpose: Lets the user see whether each project is on track.
why: Likely reason: a burndown chart compares planned progress with actual progress, which the header text describes.
how: Reads all projects from the store. For each one, shows its name, a risk badge (low, medium or high), its velocity, its description, a completion bar, and a line chart with an ideal line and an actual line. If there are no projects, shows a message instead.
inputs: Project records from the store, including risk level, velocity, progress percent and burndown data.
outputs: Cards and charts on screen. Nothing is saved from this page.
risks: A risk level outside low, medium or high has no matching badge colour. Charts stay empty if the burndown data does not use the day, ideal and actual fields. Missing velocity is shown as zero.
debug: If a card has no chart, check the burndown data on that project. If a badge is wrong, check the risk level value. If velocity shows zero, check that the field is set.
